question: Can exact search raise its throughput (support queries answered per step) enough to finish worlds at 12 states, without any false certificate?

motivation.label: Observed (study 028) / Inferred (cause)
observed: S3 capped every query at <=10.03 s (GQB pass) but U at 12 states stayed equal to S2 (0.398 vs 0.399; diff -0.001 [-0.020, 0.019])
X(S3)=0/12 at 12 and 16 states; >98% of S3 UNKNOWNs at 12-16 states are not-run queries, under 2% solver UNKNOWN
S3 solve_support uses about 52 s of the 55 s step budget at 12-16 states
S1 beats both exact arms on X at 8 states (7/12) and 12 states (3/12) but makes 3 false certificates on stress
motivation.inferred: The limit is the number and per-call cost of support queries, not single-query overruns

arms.S4: S3 plus throughput changes: (i) one incremental solver per step with assumption literals instead of a fresh solve per query; (ii) witness reuse, where a model found for one query is checked against later queries before solving; (iii) query batching, where k open queries are decided by one solve over a disjunction, splitting only on SAT

design.same_budget: 55 s per step, 10 s per query cap, as in study 028
design.soundness: every S4 certificate rechecked by the frozen exact reference; any mismatch with S2/S3 truth on an answered query is a FAIL

heldout_ranges.note: Fresh ranges following the study-number convention (028 used 94x0001). Disjoint from every earlier plan. Drawn only after a ledgered seedcheck_029.
